speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you very much, Madam Clerk. I just want to welcome everybody to our August meeting. Before we get going, I wanted to take the opportunity to communicate two messages to the community. And the first message I want to communicate is with respect to vaccinations and vaccines. We're doing pretty well in the Algoma District. And our vaccination rate is healthy. But the reality is that we want to see it improve. And we want to see more people in the Algoma region, particularly in Sault Ste. Marie, receive their vaccine. We have kids starting school again in September. A large number of those children who will be attending school cannot be vaccinated. So they'll be in classrooms. They'll be in close quarters. They'll be in congregate settings. And one of the ways that we can help keep our kids safe is by getting the vaccinations ourselves. So for all of you who have got it, your first and second dose, thank you. For those of you who have not, as a matter of convenience, we have a number of doses. They're very easy to get. We have significant pop-up clinics, walk-in clinics. And you can really get your vaccine without much effort or challenge. And for those of you that are concerned about it or have some hesitancy, I respect that. But I would encourage you to learn about it, to solicit expert advice on it, to solicit medical advice on it, to not get your advice, your information from social media, but get it from people that study this and know what they are doing and what they are talking about and consider it. Because the more of us that get vaccinated, the safer that we keep ourselves, our family, our friends, and our community at large. So I'd encourage you to consider that and move forward with it. The other point I wanted to make and comment I want to take before we start our meeting is the community is largely aware that we welcomed just under 100 guests from North Spirit-like First Nation. And those guests have all returned home back to their First Nation. And I had the privilege of meeting a number of people that came here from North Spirit Lake. I went up to the water tower where they were staying, a few different occasions. And on the last occasion, I walked in just to check on the folks before they were leaving the next day. And one of the elders recognized me from my previous visits and pulled me aside. And in the seven years that I've been the mayor of a community, the conversation I had with him was one of the most special I had and really one of the, he created a significant amount of pride in our community. He, you know, I'll say some of the conversation for me and him personally, but he told me that he had never been to a place like Sault Ste. Marie and he had never been treated the way he was treated in Sault Ste. Marie. And he remarked on the kindness of all the people from Sault Ste. Marie that he interacted with. And he remarked on how he was treated and how members of his community was treated and how grateful he was for Sault Ste. Marie, referring to it as now a second home. So it was a really touching conversation and it left me feeling a tremendous measure of pride for the effort that was put together. So I wanna just give the community some scope of that effort so that you can share in kind of the positive feelings that I have and the gratefulness that I have to all the people that contributed. So I'm just gonna go through a list of the organizations that participated in welcoming the good folks in North Spirit Lake First Nation and taking care of them while they were here. I wanna start with the Water Tower and thanking them for their leadership and embracing this project and the evacuees. I wanna recognize JJ and Donna. I wanna recognize you two for your leadership and your team at the Water Tower. They were tremendous. City staff, we had staff from City Transit, Community Service, Cemeteries, Communications. Specifically, I wanna recognize the CAO who led the initiative and really our Emergency Management staff, Lauren Perry and Naomi Thibault were exceptional. So the city staff were fantastic. We had support from Sioux Police, Social Services, Ontario Health, Garden River First Nation. I wanna recognize Chief Ricard and his team for the significant effort they made to welcome our guests. David Jones from Spirit of Concepts, Batchewana First Nations, Cathy and the whole team at the Indigenous Friendship Centre, Interior Aboriginal Housing, Dr. Wendeman, APH, Red Cross, Sioux Area Hospital, the Clean Team Laundry at Sioux Area Hospital. And then we had Superior Family Health Team, the Algoma Nurse Practitioner-led Clinic, Algoma District Medical Group, the Group Health Centre, Men Oasin, North Shore Health Services, Inc. And then a whole list of organizations in the community that donated their time, their effort and items to support the group that was here. It was an exceptional project with a tremendous amount of community collaboration. And the team that worked on this succeeded 1000%. They made Sioux St. Marie look great and they certainly made our guests feel great. So I wanna just recognize that work and I wanna thank them deeply for it as the mayor. And I understand that the federal and provincial agencies that participated and oversaw the work were impressed themselves and are gonna take some best practices from what happened here and apply those practices to other communities when other evacuations have to occur. So job exceptionally well done to everybody who participated and you have our collective gratitude for doing a great job. So before we get into the meeting, I wanna acknowledge with respect that we are in Robinson here on treaty territory, that the land on which we are gathered is traditional territory in Anishinaabe, home of Garden River First Nation, Batchewana First Nation and the historic Sioux St. Marie Métis Council. I also wanna recognize the Indigenous Friendship Center, our urban Aboriginal population and acknowledge that this area is historically known as Bauteng. Madam Clerk, if we could start our meeting, please.
